name: dialog
pattern: A modal dialog using native HTMLDialogElement and a non-modal dialog that moves and resizes within a container
responsibility: Provides dialog opening and closing, ARIA, focus return, keyboard operations, close reasons, and non-modal bounds and state output. The user manages elements, content, layout, and stacking order

targets.dialog: One native <dialog> with data-dialog-target="dialog" inside the root
targets.trigger: At least one native <button type="button"> with data-dialog-target="trigger" inside the root
targets.close: Zero or more native <button type="button"> elements with data-dialog-target="close" inside the root
targets.title: A title displayed in the dialog with data-dialog-target="title"; zero or one inside the root
targets.container: Required once for non-modal. The dialog's parent element. Use a dimensioned positioning area without border or padding and create the containing block with user CSS. Scrolling, rotation/skew, and vertical writing are outside the scope
targets.move: Required once for non-modal. A native button[type=button] with an accessible name inside the dialog, used for movement drag and arrow operations
targets.resize: Required once for non-modal. A native button[type=button] with an accessible name inside the dialog, used to resize toward inline-end / the bottom edge
targets.xControl: Required once for non-modal. A labeled native input[type=number] inside the dialog for entering the position percentage from inline-start
targets.yControl: Required once for non-modal. A labeled native input[type=number] inside the dialog for entering the position percentage from the top edge
targets.widthControl: Required once for non-modal. A labeled native input[type=number] inside the dialog for entering the width percentage
targets.heightControl: Required once for non-modal. A labeled native input[type=number] inside the dialog for entering the height percentage
targets.apply: Required once for non-modal. A native button[type=button] with an accessible name inside the dialog that applies all four inputs together. Software keyboard and tap can reach the same bounds as drag
targets.instructions: Required once for non-modal. Non-empty operation instructions inside the dialog describing movement and resize arrows, Shift, Escape, numeric input, and apply. The controller composes its ID into aria-describedby for move and resize

authorMarkup.label: The dialog has an accessible name from a non-empty aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title target. The controller supplements aria-labelledby only when a title target exists and neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby exists
authorMarkup.validity: A root has exactly one native <dialog> and at least one trigger; triggers and close targets are native button[type=button]. Non-modal configurations have one of each additional target, all as distinct elements. Make dialog a direct child of container, with dialog and container using the same direction and horizontal-tb. Non-modal role may be omitted or dialog; aria-modal may be omitted or false; closedby may be omitted or none. Additional controls must not be synchronized by disabled, readonly, or form submit/reset. Do not add additional targets to modal configurations
authorMarkup.content: The controller does not generate or manage elements, content, backdrop, scroll lock, or z-index. Non-modal CSS applies dialog border-box position and dimensions from custom properties and removes margin and native max-size constraints. The user provides overflow and minimum dimensions that keep content and operation paths reachable even for a small rectangle. Set touch-action:none on handles

semanticElements: The dialog target must be an HTMLDialogElement
Trigger and close targets must be HTMLButtonElement with type="button"
The title target must be a descendant of dialog
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate on connection and target replacement. When invalid, disable enhancement and call console.warn once per root while connected. Do not apply ARIA, state output, or native open to initially invalid markup. If valid non-modal markup becomes invalid, cancel the preview, close the original dialog without notification, synchronize the last valid trigger and root/dialog state to closed, and then remove listeners. Do not apply attributes to newly added invalid elements. Do not throw
contractValidation.warning: The warning includes the violating element type and controller name. Validate again after the user repairs and reconnects the markup

attributes: step=any and required on non-modal xControl / yControl / widthControl / heightControl
completion.warning: List completed attributes using "Added <attributes>. Include them in your markup." Warn once per connection using a flag separate from the enhancement-disabling warning.

completionExempt: Composing the instructions id into move / resize aria-describedby
Synchronizing non-modal custom properties and input.value

open.description: Initial open state. When true, open on connection according to the modal setting

modal.description: false is non-modal. A change while connected closes the current dialog without notification, revalidates, and opens according to open value

x.description: Initial inline-start position percentage. A finite number

y.description: Initial top-edge position percentage. A finite number

width.description: Initial width percentage. A finite number

height.description: Initial height percentage. A finite number

minWidth.description: Minimum width percentage. Greater than 0 and at most 100

minHeight.description: Minimum height percentage. Greater than 0 and at most 100

step.description: Percentage for one handle arrow operation. Greater than 0 and at most 100. Shift multiplies it by 10

bounds.type: DialogBounds = { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }
bounds.description: A copy of committed non-modal bounds. The setter accepts four finite numbers, clamps dimensions from the minimum to 100, and positions from 0 to 100−dimension. It discards drag without notification. Invalid values, modal state, and disconnection are no-ops. Values are initial settings and are not changed by operations

open.description: Current open state. Like show()/close(), the setter commits state programmatically without dispatching an event

show().description: Open with native showModal() when modal=true and native show() when false. Synchronize ARIA and state output without dispatching an event

close(returnValue).description: Close with dialog.close(returnValue). returnValue is an empty string when omitted, and no event is dispatched

toggle().description: Toggle the current open state. Execute programmatically without dispatching an event

dialog:beforechange.when: Immediately before committing bounds from a non-modal trusted handle arrow, drag pointerup, or apply activation
dialog:beforechange.effect: preventDefault stops commitment and change and restores the preview and inputs to committed bounds. Do not commit an old request if the listener changes the API, settings, targets, or open state. Do not accept mutations to detail

dialog:change.when: After a non-modal bounds change is committed. Use the same DialogChangeDetail as beforechange

dialog:beforeopen.when: Immediately before native open from trusted trigger activation
dialog:beforeopen.effect: When preventDefault() is called, do not open or change focus or state output

dialog:open.when: After opening through trusted trigger activation is committed

dialog:beforeclose.when: Immediately before closing from trusted close-button activation or Escape

detail.returnValue: The returnValue about to be committed. Usually an empty string

dialog:beforeclose.effect: When preventDefault() is called, do not close or change focus inside the dialog

dialog:close.when: After closing from trusted close-button activation or Escape is committed

events.programmatic: The open setter, show(), close(), toggle(), initialization, reconnection, disconnect(), and dynamic target synchronization do not dispatch events
events.sameState: Trigger activation while already open, close activation while already closed, and activation of a disabled target do not dispatch events
events.formMethodDialog: Close from <form method="dialog"> and backdrop clicks are outside the scope; use a close target or the public API

consumerIntegration.stimulusActions: Specify data-action="dialog:open->controller#method dialog:close->controller#method" on the root or an ancestor. Ordinary trigger/close click actions can also be used; the controller does not stop event propagation
consumerIntegration.cancelableHook: To stop close, call event.preventDefault() with data-action="dialog:beforeclose->controller#method". To stop open, use dialog:beforeopen
consumerIntegration.programmatic: Another controller can call open/show/close/toggle through a Stimulus controller reference or outlets. The programmatic API does not dispatch events
consumerIntegration.nested: When receiving events from a nested dialog outside, narrow them to your root with the data-action :self modifier or event.target === event.currentTarget

initial: When open value is false, make the dialog closed
When open value is true, open after connection according to the modal setting
When the dialog is already natively open, do not call showModal() twice; synchronize only open state and state output
behavior.trigger: A trusted click on an enabled trigger opens through dialog:beforeopen with pointer or keyboard reason. Ignore disabled triggers
behavior.close: A trusted click on an enabled close target closes through dialog:beforeclose with pointer or keyboard reason. Ignore disabled close targets
behavior.escape: Receive the native dialog cancel event and close as Escape through dialog:beforeclose. If beforeclose is canceled, also call preventDefault() on the cancel event
behavior.returnValue: The public close(returnValue) passes the specified value to native dialog.close(). A user-operation close has an empty returnValue; form method="dialog" returnValue is outside the scope
behavior.modal: For modal=true, use showModal() and the native top layer, inert, and focus containment. For false, use native show() and allow background operation and Tab entry/exit. Do not provide a custom focus trap or foreground switching among multiple panels
behavior.bounds: Non-modal bounds are percentages relative to container. x is inline-start and y is the top edge. Clamp width and height from their minimums to 100, then clamp positions from 0 to 100−dimension. Movement preserves dimensions; resize preserves position and is limited to the remaining area. Reconnection and coordinate-value changes reapply all four coordinate values; min / step changes normalize the current value. Preserve percentages when container dimensions change and do not change focus or events
behavior.drag: Accept only primary pointer button=0 and use pointer capture on the handle. pointermove previews CSS and inputs without changing the bounds getter or events. Dispatch beforechange/change once on pointerup. Do not notify for equal values. Discard the preview on pointercancel, lostpointercapture, Escape, blur, disconnection, or target, settings, or public API changes. Ignore other pointers and synthetic events. Also discard it if container dimensions or direction change during drag
behavior.inputs: Delegate editing of the inputs themselves to native behavior and validate and commit all four values on trusted apply activation. Report empty, non-finite, and custom-validity violations with native reportValidity and do not apply them. Use the same normalization as the bounds setter. Do not set control min/max; supplement step=any. Prevent form submission from Enter on additional inputs. The user owns native form submission values and reset
behavior.backdrop: Do not close on backdrop clicks. User CSS and markup own the backdrop appearance and the cue for clicking it

keyboard.nativeDialog: Delegate modal Tab and Shift+Tab focus containment and Escape dispatch to native behavior. Non-modal dialogs allow Tab and Shift+Tab entry and exit and treat only Escape inside the dialog as a cancelable close. Escape during drag cancels the drag without closing. Do not process Escape when a child widget called preventDefault

panel.ArrowLeft: move goes visually left; resize shrinks in LTR and grows in RTL
panel.ArrowRight: move goes visually right; resize grows in LTR and shrinks in RTL
panel.ArrowUp: move goes up; resize reduces height
panel.ArrowDown: move goes down; resize increases height
panel.Escape: Cancel drag; otherwise close the non-modal dialog containing focus
panel.Enter: Native activation of the apply button. Prevent form submission on additional inputs
panel.Space: Native activation of the apply button
panel.modifiers: Ignore handle operations with Ctrl, Alt, Meta, or IME

focus.open: Native showModal()/show() determines initial focus. Follow autofocus and native focus rules
focus.close: For modal dialogs, return focus to the last originating trigger when it remains connected and enabled. For non-modal dialogs, defer focus return to native close and do not steal focus that moved to the background before closing
focus.programmatic: The controller does not move focus for public API calls, initialization, reconnection, or canceled before events. Preserve the focus behavior of native show/close

dialog: Use the implicit role and display semantics of native <dialog>; do not add role or aria-modal
When id is absent, add an id unique within the document
trigger: When aria-controls is absent, add the dialog id
Synchronize aria-expanded with the open state as a controller-owned state output
managedMarkup.title: When a title target exists and the dialog has neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby, assign a title id and add aria-labelledby
managedMarkup.preservation: Do not overwrite an authored id, role, aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-modal, aria-controls, or other static attribute. Respect native dialog semantics and synchronize controller-owned aria-expanded, data-state, native open, non-modal input.value, and bounds custom properties
managedMarkup.disabled: Read only the native disabled attributes of trigger and close targets as activation guards. Do not add data-* attributes for disabled state

stateOutputs.bounds: Output --dialog-x, --dialog-y, --dialog-width, and --dialog-height as unitless percentages on non-modal dialogs. Output a preview during drag and committed bounds otherwise. Remove them when switching to modal. Do not set CSS position or dimension properties directly
stateOutputs.ownership: The root, dialog, and trigger data-state attributes and trigger aria-expanded are controller-owned

lifecycle: Register root click, keydown, pointerdown/move/up/cancel, and lostpointercapture listeners plus window blur and dialog cancel/close listeners in connect(), and remove them in disconnect(). Do not register twice after reconnection. Also release drag pointer capture and preview
In disconnect(), close an open native dialog to release the top layer and modal state without dispatching an event
Leave generated attributes and state outputs in place on disconnect().
On reconnection, synchronize structural attributes and state output with the current markup and open value
Track every target addition and removal with Stimulus TargetConnected/TargetDisconnected, and synchronously check membership during non-modal operations
Do not throw when a target is temporarily absent.

observations.environment: macOS Safari + VoiceOver and touch devices
observations.item: Native dialog roles/names, non-modal entry/exit, number-input values, handle instructions, touch dragging, and software-keyboard entry
observations.impact: Native dialog/button/number-input semantics and equivalent controls are fixed independently of compatibility wording and touch ergonomics.

acceptanceCriteria: Required AAA criteria: 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception), with no pointer-only features; and 3.2.5 Change on Request, with controller focus movement limited to user actions or consumer JS calls, never timers.
Do not partially apply ARIA to compensate for semantic HTML contract violations; detect them with console.warn and disabled enhancement
Require WCAG 2.2 Level AA for every configuration, preserving the native <dialog> role, name, relationship to triggers, and open state. Modal dialogs conform to the APG Dialog (Modal) Pattern

Use the native showModal() top layer, inert behavior, and focus containment for modal dialogs. Use native show() for non-modal dialogs so the background remains operable. Do not implement a custom focus trap or scroll lock
Only trusted trigger/close/Escape operations and trusted non-modal drag/keyboard/apply bounds changes dispatch one cancelable before event followed by one committed event in order
Canceling a before event stops opening/closing and controller-managed focus return
Public API calls, initialization, reconnection, and disconnect do not dispatch events; they synchronize open, native dialog.open, and state output
Preserve existing id and ARIA attributes, and ensure generated ids do not collide within the same document
After modal close, return focus to the valid originating trigger. For non-modal dialogs, defer focus return to native behavior and do not steal focus that moved to the background
Pass automated tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.

Test non-modal background operation, Tab entry/exit, preservation of external focus, boundaries, RTL, and equivalent drag / keyboard / numeric-input-and-apply paths for movement and resize in all three engines

Observation: verify native dialog role/name, non-modal entry/exit, number-input values, and handle instructions with macOS Safari + VoiceOver. The public specification is based on native dialog/button/number-input semantics and operation instructions and does not depend on this compatibility observation. Real-device verification is pending. Real-device touch dragging and software-keyboard input are also unverified observations
